{{Short description|Topological manifold in mathematics}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''E''<sub>8</sub> manifold}}
In [[low-dimensional topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''''E''<sub>8</sub> manifold''' is the unique [[Compact space|compact]], [[simply connected]] topological [[4-manifold]] with [[Intersection form (4-manifold)|intersection form]] the [[E8 lattice|''E''<sub>8</sub> lattice]].

==History==

The <math>E_8</math> manifold was discovered by [[Michael Freedman]] in 1982.  [[Rokhlin's theorem]] shows that it has no [[smooth structure]] (as does [[Donaldson's theorem]]), and in fact, combined with the work of [[Andrew Casson]] on the [[Casson invariant]], this shows that the <math>E_8</math> manifold is not even [[Triangulation (topology)|triangulable]] as a [[simplicial complex]].

==Construction==

The manifold can be constructed by first plumbing together disc bundles of [[Euler number (topology)|Euler number]] 2 over the [[sphere]], according to the [[Dynkin diagram]] for <math>E_8</math>. This results in <math>P_{E_8}</math>, a 4-manifold whose boundary is homeomorphic to the [[Poincaré homology sphere]].  Freedman's theorem on [[fake 4-ball]]s then says we can cap off this homology sphere with a fake 4-ball to obtain the <math>E_8</math> manifold.

== Properties ==

* <math>
M_{E_8}\times S^n
</math> and <math>
M_{E_8}\times T^n
</math> have no smooth structure (and not even a PL structure) for any <math>
n\geq 0
</math>.<ref>Scorpan 05, p. 219–220</ref>

== Connected sums ==
[[Freedman classification|Freedman's classification]]<ref name=":0">Scorpan 05, p. 240–244</ref> yields the following three orientation-preserving homeomorphisms between [[Connected sum|connected sums]] of the '''<math>E_8</math>'''-manifold <math>
M_{E_8}
</math>, the orientation-reversed '''<math>E_8</math>'''-manifold <math>
\overline{M_{E_8}}
</math>, fake second complex projective space <math>
*\mathbb{C}P^2
</math> and the K3 surface <math>
\mathrm{K3}
</math> (solutions of <math>
x^4+y^4+z^4+w^4=0
</math> in [[twistor space]] <math>
\mathbb{C}P^3
</math>):<ref name=":0" />

: <math>
\overline{M_{E_8}}\#*\mathbb{C}P^2
\cong\mathbb{C}P^2\#8\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2};
</math>
: <math>
M_{E_8}\#\overline{M_{E_8}}
\cong\#8(S^2\times S^2);
</math>
: <math>
2\overline{M_{E_8}}\#3(S^2\times S^2)
\cong\mathrm{K3}.
</math>

Required are the isomorphisms of their intersection forms: <math>
-E_8\oplus[+1]\cong[+1]\oplus8[-1]
</math> follows from [[Serre classification|Serre's classification]],<ref>Scorpan 05, p. 238</ref> furthermore <math>
E_8\oplus-E_8\cong 8\begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1 \\
1 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
</math> and <math>
Q_\mathrm{K3}\cong -2E_8\oplus 3\begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1 \\
1 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
</math>. In the above homeomorphisms, <math>
\mathbb{C}P^2\#8\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}
</math> is the [[complex surface]] underlying the [[Barlow surface]], an exotic smooth structure. Now the above connected sums show, that even though the left sides have no canonical smooth structure (hence cannot give any [[diffeomorphism]]), these are smoothable just like the right sides and potentially even in multiple ways.
